notes: Purely a jurisdictional dispute (County Court vs. new City Court) over a disorderly-house indictment; does not address letting, lodging, or boarding-house regulation on the merits.
Retail liquor licensing/local-option constitutional challenge; unrelated to letting rooms or dwellings for occupancy.
Concerns validity of a city ordinance defining and prohibiting 'variety shows' as tied to bawdy-house/disorderly-house statutes; not about renting rooms/dwellings to lodgers or boarders.
Rape/nonage appeal; a 'rent house' is mentioned only as a locational landmark near the assault site, with no discussion of letting or lodging law.
Upholds a city ordinance prohibiting liquor sales in variety theaters; concerns theater/liquor regulation, not letting of dwellings or rooms.

holding_summary: In a burglary prosecution, where a house had two rooms separated by a partition and the alleged owner rented the whole house but let the other room to a subtenant, the room she occupied and exclusively controlled was properly alleged as her 'house.' The court treated the sub-letting arrangement as an ordinary tenancy that did not create joint ownership of either room.

quotes.text: The entire house had been rented by Amanda Isom, and Lula Smith was her tenant of one of the rooms.
Under this state of case, Amanda Isom was the owner of the room burglarized, and the fact that she rented to Lula Smith the other room did not make them joint tenants of Amanda’s room.
The entire house had been rented by Amanda Isom, and Lula Smith was her tenant of one of the rooms.

notes: Householder rented a two-room house and let one room to a subtenant; court treats the arrangement as an ordinary, legally recognized tenancy giving each occupant possessory ownership of her own room.
Validity of a town's Sunday-closing ordinance as applied to a merchant selling whisky; no bearing on letting dwellings or rooms.
Concerns a state agent's authority to lease vacant State land (sand/gravel bar) under a specific statute; a real-property leasing dispute unrelated to dwelling/room occupancy by lodgers or boarders.
Invalidates a municipal 'curfew ordinance' restricting minors' presence on streets at night; no connection to letting or lodging.

Discusses tenant-at-will possessory rights ('a tenant in possession of such premises is the owner thereof until the expiration of the lease') but in the context of an ordinary farm/agricultural tenancy dispute over a pistol-carrying charge, not short-term letting of rooms/dwellings to lodgers or boarders.

Murder appeal turning on special-venire/jury-panel irregularities; mentions defendant renting part of his farm to the deceased only as background, with no legal discussion of letting or lodging.
City ordinance authorizing police to shoot unmuzzled dogs held void; concerns property/police-power doctrine as to animals, unrelated to letting dwellings or rooms.

Murder appeal; defendant's own testimony mentions boarding his wife 'at a boarding house the first week she was in Denison at $5 per week' and a 'section boarding house' keeper, but these are incidental factual details in an alibi/insanity case, not a holding on lodging or boarding-house law.
Habeas corpus over militia draft eligibility of a wartime refugee; discusses 'sojourner'/'temporary resident' in the context of domicile for militia duty, not letting of dwellings or rooms.
